- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks and shift toward mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects downward; cap overshoots and apply lagged sentiment damping.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.67+ for 3+ days), model frequently overestimates; apply downward bias to high-forecast periods.
- When true outcomes show strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive low values), model often fails to adjust; use sentiment history to trigger early correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or positive; apply smoothing or decay to initial forecast values.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (alternating 0.33–1.00), model exhibits erratic behavior; use sentiment-weighted moving average to stabilize forecasts.
